ratings_why.fun: Folding sale into death makes one set of triggers work in shop and fight, and pieces stack in ways the builds don't list, like Undertaker killing a Fruit unit with Pallbearer and Cordwainer out.
ratings_why.distinct: Sell-equals-death and the funeral-order puzzle are fresh, but the core of 'summon X/X tokens off deaths' is close to a familiar deathrattle tribe.

verdict_why: One real rules gap: Old Fingers' copies don't say whether they last only the fight, and if they stay, they can be sold into the loop.

points.text: Old Fingers' copies don't say how long they last. Sprouts made in a fight last the fight; say the same for the copies, or they become free units that can be sold each turn.
Old Fingers' own copies dying become 'the last 2 non-Sprout units laid to rest', so he keeps digging up his own copies. Say whether copies count for his list.
Undertaker plus a Fruit unit plus Pallbearer and Cordwainer turns one Start of Combat kill into his Attack plus two half-stat Sprouts. Worth naming in the builds; it is the tribe's best hidden combo.
Hired Mute only counts. Make it positional, e.g. it grows more when a unit beside it is laid to rest, so it joins the funeral-order puzzle.
Foxfire Lamplighter is a plain counter reader. It could spend Register count or care about which slot died, to give a choice instead of a passive number.

standouts.why: A self-kill that feeds Fruit, Pallbearer, Cordwainer, Inkcap and Ooze Bellies; many uses beyond its stated job.
A buffer that is also a fuse; Health buffs become fuel and Hedgerow Pass can keep it alive on purpose.
Granting Fruit to other tribes' units (or to Ludwig, who can't be sold but can die) is the Johnny door the tribe promises.

weakest.why: Counts deaths and gains Attack; nothing to decide.
A flat Sprout aura that Grandmother Bootlace does better.
Reads the Register passively; no interaction with order or slots.

flags.note: Copies' lifetime is not stated, and whether his own copies refill his 'last 2' list.
With Bootlace Cordwainer each Sprout death makes two Fruit Sprouts; check whether 'six times a fight' counts triggers or Sprouts, and golden doubles it.
Shop Sprouts stay and are Guild units, so they bank Bellows' +1/+1 three times a turn on cheap bodies.
